refsynopsisdiv.title: Syntax
refsynopsisdiv.synopsis: [pks, loc] = findpeaks(data) [pks, loc, extra] = findpeaks(data) [pks, loc, extra] = findpeaks(data, "PropertyName", PropertyValue) [pks, loc, extra] = findpeaks(data, "DoubleSided")

listitem.para: Vector. The input signal to analyze. Must be a single column vector with at least 3 elements.
Vector. The values of the peaks in the input signal.
Vector. The indices of the peaks in the input signal.
Structure. Contains additional information about the peaks:
Structure containing the parabola fitted to each peak.
Baseline height at which the roots of the peaks were calculated.
Abscissa values at which the parabola fitted to each peak realizes its width.
Minimum peak height (non-negative scalar). Default is `eps`.
Minimum separation between peaks (positive integer). Default is 1.
Minimum width of peaks (positive integer). Default is 1.
Maximum width of peaks (positive integer). Default is `Inf`.
Indicates that the data contains both positive and negative values. The baseline is taken as the mean value of the data.

refsection.title: Description
refsection.para: This function identifies peaks in the input signal `data`. Peaks are defined as local maxima for positive data or maxima/minima for double-sided data. The function supports additional options to filter peaks based on height, distance, and width.
